..
A developing monsoon trough to the southwest of the Marianas is 
pushing occasionally scattered showers into the region along with 
southeasterly winds. This disturbance is expected to keep its 
distance and keep the Marianas dry overall for the next few days.
Guam may receive slightly more rainfall due to its closer proximity 
to the monsoon feature. Light to gentle winds may also allow for 
island effect showers for Guam tomorrow, though likely remaining 
isolated to over or just offshore of Agat and Apra Harbor. Isolated 
thunderstorms will be possible as soon as Tuesday night, 
particularly if the monsoon trough strengthens more than expected. 
Models indicate the trough pushing away to the west and being 
replaced by a new weak trough sometime Thursday which may bring in 
more scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms to the Marianas. 
Minor island effect remains possible for central and northeast Guam 
Wednesday, potentially becoming more significant Thursday and 
spreading to all islands as models indicate a further decrease in 
winds.

Marine...
Light southeasterlies will become easterly late tonight, only
increasing to light to gentle during the day tomorrow. Combined seas
of 3 to 4 feet may increase slightly starting Tuesday night with an 
increase in southwest monsoon swell, possibly peaking Wednesday. A 
low risk of rip currents will continue along all reefs before west 
and/or south facing reefs potentially become moderate Tuesday night.
Scattered showers and isolated thunderstorms are possible by Tuesday
night, with at least isolated thunderstorms continuing through the 
weekend. Therefore, A moderate risk of lightning is possible Tuesday 
night and continuing through the weekend for all beaches.

Eastern Micronesia...
Pohnpei and Kosrae sit along the far northern outskirts of a broad 
buffer circulation centered south of the Equator. Satellite this 
afternoon shows patches of scattered showers racing eastward to 
southeastward across Pohnpei and Kosrae coastal waters, associated 
with convergent northwesterly inflow into the distant buffer 
circulation. To the east, patchy scattered showers are seen across 
eastern portions of the RMI within a weak surface circulation located
just southeast of Majuro. This circulation connects to another weak 
disturbance to the northeast across the Date Line, and to the broad 
monsoon trough that extends across much of Micronesia. These features
will maintain scattered showers in the forecast for Pohnpei, Kosrae,
and Majuro through Tuesday, before a quiet doldrum-like pattern sets
up around Tuesday night through Thursday. Wetter conditions resume 
toward the end of the week, mainly for Pohnpei and Kosrae, as 
convergence increases across the area along the far northern edge of
the northward-lifting buffer circulation. Altimetry data shows
combined seas between 3 and 6 feet across much of the region,
comprised mainly of a southeast swell emanating from distant 
features in the Southern Hemisphere, with a light, secondary west to
south-southwest swell. Seas may see a gradual, slight diminishing by
the end of the week as these swells subside.

Western Micronesia...
For Palau and Yap, a Special Weather Statement remains in effect
for the developing monsoon pattern. This pattern is producing up to 
fresh to strong winds over the next several days. Numerous to 
widespread locally heavy showers are to be expected this week. Model
guidance suggests 3 to 5 inches through the middle of the week, and
an additional 2 to 4 inches through the latter half of the week,
totaling 6 to 9 inches by the weekend. If these showers develop as 
expected, soils will become saturated enough to pose a risk for 
mudslides toward the end of the week. At this time, the risk remains 
low. As the monsoon pattern continues to develop, winds and seas will
increase, but are expected to remain below conditions hazardous to
small craft. As a tropical disturbance embedded within the monsoon
trough attempts to consolidate, it will move north and carry the bulk
of the convective monsoon with it, easing the showers and winds near
Palau and Yap as early as Saturday.

For Chuuk, the remains of what was Invest 90W are expected to bring 
in one more influx of moisture to the lagoon. To reflect this 
numerous showers are expected for Tuesday. This is expected to be the
last hurrah. Less than an inch of rain is anticipated. Then, a drier
weather pattern is expected to set up. Seas near Chuuk are expected 
to remain benign at 3 to 4 feet through the week.
